title: Thousand Needles
body: Thousand Needles is a deep canyon in southern Kalimdor, lying below the cliffs at the southern edge of the Barrens and running east to salt flats on the border of Tanaris, with Feralas beyond its western rim. It takes its name from the dozens of tall columns of sandstone that rise from the dry canyon floor. Tauren make their homes on the high mesas, out of reach of the centaur war bands below, climbing to them by lifts and crossing between the spires on rope bridges. The Great Lift carries travelers down from the Barrens, and the Horde holds Freewind Post high atop a mesa. The Galak centaur raid from Camp E'thok and Splithoof Crag, a band of the Grimtotem tribe keeps its secrets on Darkcloud Pinnacle, harpies screech in the western ravines and wyverns nest at Highperch. In the east lie the Shimmering Flats, a blinding salt plain below the level of the sea, where gnomes and goblins race rocket cars and dwarves dug too deep and woke a silithid hive.

title: The Great Lift
body: At the southern edge of the Barrens the land drops away in sheer cliffs, and the Great Lift, an elevator built by the tauren, carries travelers down to the floor of Thousand Needles. Tauren braves keep watch over it. Brave Moonhorn warns that the centaurs have stepped up their attacks and that the nearby Grimtotem have been acting strangely. Grish Longrunner has guarded the lift so long that he wants only leave to visit his family. Not far away lies the body of a dwarf, Henrig Lonebrow, his weathered journal still with him. Its pages tell of the boar men of Razorfen Kraul who took him captive, and of the dying night elf who shared his cell.

title: Darkcloud Pinnacle
body: East of the Great Lift, three small mesas form Darkcloud Pinnacle, home of a band of the Grimtotem tribe. Rope bridges join the mesas, and the only two ways in are well guarded. Stompers, geomancers and bandits hold its heights, the fearsome Harb Foulmountain roams among them, and the outcast Arnak Grimtotem holds a strange sway over the clan. The Grimtotem here keep secrets. Agents of unknown origin have visited them, and hidden letters speak of an alliance that must be kept from the other tribes. On an isolated needle where the tribe lays its dead rests the dormant Sacred Fire of Life. Nearby lies the Boiling Pool, where elementals stir and the rare Incendia agave grows.

title: Camp E'thok
body: Camp E'thok is a camp of the Galak centaur in the northwest of the canyon, not far from the road that runs past Whitereach Post. From here the centaurs strike at caravans and travelers on the road, and the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner was the only one to live through their attack on his. Stormers, maulers and marauders hold the camp, ready to ride out at a moment's notice. Pesterhide hyenas skulk about the camp as well, among them Steelsnap, the tyrant of the pack, whom the hunters of Thunder Bluff send their champions to slay.

title: Whitereach Post
body: Whitereach Post is a small Horde camp beside the road in the northwest of the canyon, close to Camp E'thok. The tauren Kanati Greycloud was bold enough to set up a hunting camp here, and the Galak have marked him for death because of it. Motega Firemane brought young Pao'ka Swiftmountain to Thousand Needles to study the creatures that live in these lands, and he knows the old legends of his people as well as its beasts. Laer Stepperunner sells food and drink to passing travelers. The goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner stays here too, the lone survivor of a centaur raid, tinkering with goods meant for other clients, among them a crated machine called the Robotron 3000.

title: Highperch
body: Highperch is a raised stretch of the far western canyon, reached by a ramp along the canyon walls northwest of Freewind Post, and it is the nesting ground of the proud Highperch wyverns. Patriarchs, consorts and soarers guard nests full of eggs, sun scorched shells lie among the rocks, and the rare Heartrazor hunts here. The Horde prizes these beasts. At Freewind Post the apprentice Elu gathers Highperch eggs, since the master wind riders cannot train wyverns fast enough to keep up with the demand. Those who come too close pay for it. Young Pao'ka Swiftmountain crept in to study the wyverns, was chased off a nest, and hid in the heights for days, lost and alone.

title: Splithoof Crag
body: Splithoof Crag is the chief village of the Galak centaur, set against the northern wall of the canyon north of Freewind Post. Scouts, wranglers and windchasers crowd its slopes, and Cliffwatcher Longhorn of Freewind sends his avengers here after the centaurs slaughtered one of his supply caravans. In the heart of the crag a heavily guarded cavern, Splithoof Hold, keeps the tribe's greatest treasure: the Cloven Hoof, a relic from the time of the centaurs' creation, held within an eternal flame. The tauren have learned that water from a night elf moonwell can douse that flame for a short while, because the dryads and the centaur share a common ancestry.

title: Freewind Post
body: Freewind Post is the Horde's stronghold in Thousand Needles, a tauren village high atop a mesa, out of reach of the centaur war bands below. Wooden lifts carry visitors up, and rope bridges span the neighboring pinnacles. Cliffwatcher Longhorn directs its defense and Freewind braves keep the watch, while an inn, the wind rider master Nyse and a handful of traders make it a welcome stop. The post has troubles enough: centaur raids, the Grimtotem of Darkcloud Pinnacle, harpies and wild serpents. Rau Cliffrunner studies the relics of the centaur, Hagar Lightninghoof chases rumors of a strange egg, and the exiled blood elf, Magistrix Elosai, seeks a cure for her people's addiction to magic.

title: The Screeching Canyon
body: West of Freewind Post the land breaks into the Screeching Canyon, a ravine overrun by screeching harpies. Roguefeathers and windcallers haunt its walls, Pesterhide hyenas prowl its floor, and kobolds of the Gravelsnout clan forage among the rocks. At its far end the harpies keep their stronghold, a cavern called the Roguefeather Den. Deep inside, the flock hoards its gathered foodstuffs. Any intruder who spoils that store soon faces the fury of the whole den, and one who survives long enough draws out Grenka Bloodscreech herself.

title: Windbreak Canyon
body: Windbreak Canyon spreads across much of the country between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats, a broad stretch of the Needles where elder cloud serpents make their nests. Needles cougars and Pesterhide snarlers hunt among the spires, and the kobold Gibblesnik is sometimes seen skulking about. The serpent dens at the foot of the cliffs may hold more than serpents. Rumor tells of a strange foreign egg hidden in one of them, guarded by the serpents as fiercely as if it were their own, though none who claim to have seen it ever got close enough to look. A ramp climbs the cliffs nearby to the hidden cave of the Weathered Nook.

title: The Weathered Nook
body: North of Freewind Post, where the cliffs look out over the needles, a ramp climbs to a small and well hidden cave called the Weathered Nook. Two tauren make their home here. Dorn Plainstalker receives those who seek to have their spirit, body and mind tested, and the first of his trials begins on planks above the canyon, with a leap that takes faith to make. Beside him lives Prate Cloudseer, a shaman whom the Horde's teachers send their most promising students to find when they are ready to take up the totem of air and learn to call upon its spirits.

title: The Shimmering Flats
body: At the eastern end of Thousand Needles the canyon opens onto the Shimmering Flats, a dried lakebed of blinding salt that lies below the level of the sea, open and almost bare of plants. Saltstone basilisks, Sparkleshell tortoises and scorpids roam the flats, vultures wheel overhead and whirling vortexes of wind wander across the salt. Wreckage lies everywhere. The gnomes and goblins who race at the Mirage Raceway crash often, and scraps of their rocket cars litter the plain for anyone willing to pick through them. The great basilisk Ironeye the Invincible and the scorpid Vile Sting stalk the flats as well, and to the south a path runs through the mountains toward Tanaris.

title: Mirage Raceway
body: Out on the Shimmering Flats lies the Mirage Raceway, a track where gnomes and goblins race their rocket cars against each other to settle whose engineering is better. The dwarf Race Master Kronkrider oversees the races and advises visitors not to bet all their money in one place, while announcers take wagers and Daisy starts the races. Gnome crews mutter that only dumb luck keeps the goblin car from crashing every race, while goblins boast of their tools and talent. Trackmaster Zherin was hired after the goblin racer Red Thunder struck a basilisk, and now keeps the beasts off the course. Vendors sell drinks, ice cream, guns and engineering supplies, and the dwarf Kravel Koalbeard deals in everything else.

title: The Rustmaul Dig Site
body: In the southwest of the Shimmering Flats lies the Rustmaul Dig Site, where dwarves of the Explorers' League were excavating until a Horde war party fell upon them and killed them all. The fighting did not end there. The diggers had broken into a cave beneath the site, and from it a swarm of silithid erupted and nearly destroyed the raiders, killing more than half their number. Now hive drones, searchers and invaders crawl over the abandoned dig, and a great silithid ravager is sometimes seen among them. A foul ooze coats the veins of mithril and truesilver that the dwarves left behind.

title: Ironstone Camp
body: Ironstone Camp is a small Horde encampment on the edge of the Shimmering Flats, where Moktar Krin and the survivors of his war party wait beside their kodos. They were sent to drive the dwarven excavators out of the Rustmaul Dig Site to the south, and they did, only to see silithid burst from the earth and kill more than half of them. Nag'zehn, Bor'zehn and Tarkreu Shadowstalker are among those left. Too battered to fight, they hold their position and wait for word from Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar, while the thunder of the races echoes off the mountain walls. Moktar counts those races as atrocities born of what the racers call science.

title: Tahonda Ruins and Weazel's Crater
body: Beyond the raceway the Shimmering Flats keep a few lonely landmarks. The Tahonda Ruins were once a tauren village, but they fell to ruin long ago and have half slipped beneath the salt and sand. No one now knows for certain why the village was abandoned. Saltstone gazers and crystalhides lurk among its broken buildings, and some suspect the basilisks themselves drove its people away. In the north of the flats lies Weazel's Crater, a large, deep pit home to more basilisks. Who or what made it is a mystery, though the scraps of rocket car scattered around it hint at one of the racers' less stable inventions.

title: Cliffwatcher Longhorn
body: Cliffwatcher Longhorn keeps watch over Freewind Post, and his patience with the enemies around him has worn thin. When centaurs raided one of his supply caravans and slaughtered everyone with it, he swore the outrage would not go unpunished and sent avengers against the Galak camp north of the post. Then came the Grimtotem. Three agents of unknown origin were seen visiting Darkcloud Pinnacle, and when their secret messages were stolen, what they revealed left him dismayed and planning for whatever may come. The bounty on the murderer Arnak Grimtotem is his to pay. After a year without writing, he is sending word of the centaurs' unrest to his brother Nataka, stationed far away at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace.

title: Arnak Grimtotem
body: Arnak Grimtotem is the Grimtotem of Darkcloud Pinnacle whom Freewind Post most wants to see dead. A wanted poster at the post names him an outcast, guilty of murder and kidnapping, offers a handsome reward to anyone brave enough to bring him to justice, and says he was last seen on the cliffs near the pinnacle. His crimes are not in doubt. He took Lakota Windsong of Freewind Post for his captive and killed her brother when he tried to stop him. Outcast or not, Lakota says he holds some strange power over the Grimtotem there, and they fight hard to keep her. Cliffwatcher Longhorn, for one, feared he would never be brought to justice.

title: Dorn Plainstalker
body: Dorn Plainstalker is a tauren sage who lives in a hidden cave in the cliffs overlooking Thousand Needles. He holds that a being is made of many facets, spirit, body and mind, and that some of them can be measured by a people's traditions while others we can only hope exist within ourselves. He considers it his duty to the young of every tribe to prepare them for the dangers they will meet once they leave the shelter of home, for too often, he says, they rush ahead before they are ready. Above all he prizes faith, and holds that it hardly matters what one believes, only that one believes in something.

title: Braug Dimspirit
body: Braug Dimspirit is a tauren shaman of great wisdom who dwells in the Stonetalon Mountains, near the mouth of the Talondeep Path. He gives the Test of Lore that Dorn Plainstalker leaves to others, and he has small regard for trials of the body, which he calls childish beside a test of the mind. The days and nights grow colder, he says, while goblins ravage the land and the night elves point fingers at the younger races, but the Forsaken and the orcs are not the only ones to blame: many of the thinking races have added to the world's pain. He questions his students on the Aspects, and on the one who became Deathwing.

title: Rok'Alim the Pounder
body: As Dorn Plainstalker tells it, in the age of the Old Gods elementals filled much of the world, worshipping those gods and held here by their power. When the Old Gods were banished, most faded away and now return only at the bidding of powerful mages. A few were strong enough to remain on their own, and Rok'Alim is one of them, a great elemental of living rock who wanders the western canyon. The centaur tribes call him the Pounder, for the thundering of his fists as he beats down any creature brave or foolish enough to stand in his path. To Dorn he is the measure of a true test of strength.

title: Wizlo Bearingshiner
body: Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin of Whitereach Post and the only survivor of a caravan the centaurs fell upon just north of the camp. The raiders took everything except his best gizmo, a hypercapacitor hanging from the neck of a rare and mighty panther, a beast so fierce that the centaurs themselves left it alone in its cage. He wants it back, though he admits he has yet to work out what it does. Wizlo will work for anyone with gold, and the exiled Magistrix Elosai is the only client he has left. For her he unpacked a Robotron 3000 he was carrying for someone else, and he dreads what that client would do if he ever found out.

title: Fizzle and Wizzle Brassbolts
body: The gnome brothers Fizzle and Wizzle Brassbolts build the gnome rocket car of the Mirage Raceway, the fastest thing on the Shimmering Flats, so fast that its pilots keep crashing. Fizzle is the dreamer, bubbling over with designs and certain that one day the car will fly, chasing fuels that burn ever hotter and engines that need pistons harder than any he can make. Wizzle is the worrier who follows behind him, building tanks his brother's fuel will not eat through and a coating to keep the car from being torn apart by its own speed. Rizzle Brassbolts pores over their newest plans. Most days they win, since the goblin car blows up so often.

title: Pozzik
body: Pozzik builds the racers of the goblin team at the Mirage Raceway, a team he calls the pride of goblins everywhere. He was one of the most respected tinkerers in Undermine before he retired to work on racers, and the first thing he did when he joined the team was develop the two engine model. Every ounce counts with him: he lightens his frames with hollow vulture bones from the salt flats, and his sponsors range from Gazlowe of Ratchet to Baron Revilgaz of Booty Bay. He is cautious enough to put a bucket of sand under his pilot's seat, which his pilot hates. That pilot, Razzeric, is the eighteenth the team has had.

title: Kravel Koalbeard
body: Kravel Koalbeard is a dwarf who has made the Shimmering Flats his marketplace. He pays for the scrap of crashed rocket cars and sells it on to gnomes and goblins forever hungry for more contraptions, and his advice comes free of charge: there is always profit to be found in someone else's tragedy. He fills special orders for the racing teams, though not always honestly, and sends deliveries as far as Stranglethorn, where Hemet Nesingwary Jr. waits on crates of special gauge ammunition and asks after crusty old Kravel, sure that he is still up to no good. The young hunter is right. Kravel's dealings with Booty Bay are the kind no pit crew would want to hear about.

title: The Four Tests
body: Dorn Plainstalker tests those who come to him in spirit, body and mind. First is a Test of Faith, a leap from the planks above Thousand Needles with no promise of survival, which shows an open mind and a spirit prepared. Next comes endurance. In the Roguefeather Den the seeker must spoil the harpies' hoarded food and outlast their fury until Grenka Bloodscreech herself comes to fight. Then strength, against Rok'Alim the Pounder, an elemental who never left the world when the Old Gods fell. The Test of Lore is not Dorn's to give. He sends his pupil north to the shaman Braug Dimspirit, who demands that the Legacy of the Aspects be fetched from the depths of Dor'danil in Ashenvale and studied, then asks which Aspect became Deathwing. Braug in turn sends the seeker to Parqual Fintallas in the Undercity, who wants a book from the Scarlet Monastery and a question answered about the creature that became the Lich King. Only then does the student return to Dorn, changed.

title: The Sacred Flame
body: The Galak centaur guard a relic from the time of their race's creation, the Cloven Hoof, kept within an eternal flame deep in Splithoof Hold. Rau Cliffrunner of Freewind Post means to have it, and he knows a way past the fire. Through his associate Zangen Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff he sends for water from a night elf moonwell. The seeker must first win an etched phial from one of the dryads near Raynewood Retreat in the heart of Ashenvale, then fill it at a moonwell on the western bank of the Falfarren River. Because dryads and centaur share an ancestry, Rau explains, the water will douse the flame, though only for a short time. With it the seeker forces a way into the Galak stronghold, past the many defenders of the crag, and takes the Cloven Hoof. Rau feels a strange energy pouring from it, and he sets to work at once on the mysteries of the centaur that it may reveal.

title: Vengeance in the Needles
body: Rumor spread through Freewind Post of a strange egg in a serpent den, guarded by the wind serpents as if it were one of their own. Hagar Lightninghoof wanted it, but when he looked closer, something burst forth that he could scarcely believe. Vengeance had come to Thousand Needles, he cried, and he sent word to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post. Motega knew the legend of Arikara and knew she must be dealt with swiftly. To call her, the dormant Sacred Fire of Life had to be lit, and for that, Incendia agave from the Boiling Pool had to be enchanted into powder by the shaman Magatha Grimtotem in Thunder Bluff. Magatha called the news grave, and yet she smiled. Cast upon the fire on the needle where the Grimtotem of Darkcloud Pinnacle bury their dead, the powder brought the serpent, and she was slain. Magatha's warning of whom Arikara hunted left Motega puzzled, but he would not doubt the most powerful shaman of his people.

title: The Centaur Raids
body: The Galak have stepped up their attacks near the Great Lift, and Brave Moonhorn sends an urgent message down the road to Freewind Post. It reaches Cliffwatcher Longhorn hard on the heels of worse news: centaurs have raided one of his supply caravans and slaughtered the whole party. He wants vengeance, and sends fighters against the Galak camp north of the post to cut down their scouts, wranglers and windchasers. The centaurs are planning a killing of their own. A Galak messenger carries their orders against Kanati Greycloud, who dared to set up a hunting camp in the Needles: the assassins will converge on his small post southwest of the Great Lift, to be rid of him and of all who might follow him. Warned in time, Kanati swears to show them how a tauren fights. Yet more of them come than he expected, and he asks for help in holding them off.

title: Free at Last
body: Arnak Grimtotem decided that Lakota Windsong of Freewind Post would be his bride. When she refused him he came back that same night and took her. Her brother tried to stop him and was slain, and Arnak carried her off to Darkcloud Pinnacle as his captive. There she waits, mourning her brother and thinking of Thalia Amberhide at Freewind, who must be sick with worry, until someone comes who will lead her out. The escape is hard won. Arnak has some strange power over the Grimtotem, Lakota warns, and they will not be happy to see her go: band after band of them falls upon her and her rescuer on the way down. Once she is free she hurries home alone. Thalia had known deep in her bones that Lakota would find her way back, and she thanks the rescuer with the belongings of Lakota's dead brother, which she knows Lakota would want them to have.

title: The Magistrix's Tonic
body: Magistrix Elosai is a sin'dorei far from Silvermoon, living on a windswept butte in Thousand Needles because her own people will no longer have her. She wrote a treatise on natural cures for the blood elves' addiction to magic, and every copy was burned. Here she can pursue her research in safety, if only someone will gather her reagents. Purifying earth comes from the thundering boulderkin of the western Needles. Her goblin associate at Whitereach Post, Wizlo Bearingshiner, supplies the rest, including water from the night elves' moonwell at Thalanaar, scooped up by a Robotron 3000 that he steers from a console hidden in the bushes on the rim of a nearby needle. Elosai mixes it all, raises a toast to a brighter future, and drinks. The tonic does not cure her. It hastens her descent toward the ranks of the Wretched, and in despair she wonders whether this is something her people must simply learn to live with.

title: Kravel's Scheme
body: Kravel Koalbeard sees profit in every corner of the Shimmering Flats. He begins as an errand runner: a parts order for the Brassbolts brothers has sat at the Ratchet docks for days, and once it is fetched he pockets one small piece before handing the rest to Fizzle, who seems none the wiser. Next he looks for leverage over the goblins. Krazek of Booty Bay spends favors and a rare bottle of elven wine to learn the secret of the goblin pilot Nazz Steamboil: he is the son of a merchant prince, hiding on the flats with a small fortune stolen from his family. Then comes the real scheme. Kravel wants something to addle the wits of a pit crew, so that their car will fall into disrepair before a race. Crank Fizzlebub of Booty Bay brews a Fool's Stout from Zanzil's zombie mixture, a crew gratefully drinks it down, and Kravel lays his bet.

title: The Indurium Race
body: Fizzle Brassbolts dreams of a fuel that burns hotter than any before, made from the salty venom of the scorpids on the flats, while his brother Wizzle fears it will eat straight through the chassis and builds new tanks from the hard shells of the flats' tortoises. A faster engine needs pistons tougher than Fizzle can make, so he writes to Martek the Exiled in the Badlands, a smith who knows metal as few others do. Martek's tests prove that indurium resists heat remarkably well, though the true ore lies deep in Uldaman. The gnome car grows faster, and across the pits the goblins notice. Pozzik is sure the Brassbolts have found a new material. While Zamek sets off a noisy distraction, someone slips off with Rizzle Brassbolts' plans, and under them, used as a paperweight, sits a lump of raw indurium. Now the goblins want their own supply from Uldaman, to keep pace with the gnomes.

title: Goblin Sponsorship
body: The goblin racing team needs every edge it can get, for the gnomes are gaining on them. Pozzik has waited weeks for a prototype fuel regulator that Gazlowe of Ratchet promised, and the trail of the missing part runs from Ratchet to the Booty Bay docks, where Wharfmaster Lozgil finds no record of it, and on to Baron Revilgaz himself. His men came back empty handed from their hunt for the blueprints, but he knows where they are: Venture Company shredders at Lake Nazferiti in Stranglethorn run on the new regulator, and their foreman Cozzle keeps the plans locked in his house. Stolen, and copied for the Baron's own notes, they reach Pozzik, who decides to rebuild the design from the ground up. His pilot Razzeric wants more. He sends for a seaforium booster from Shreev of Gadgetzan, lost when its zeppelin crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, then has the safety taken off. One slip, Shreev warns, and he will be a burnt spot on the track.
